justification: Fifteen files across the extraction path, the alerting path and a production schema change (migration 066, already applied). Two of the changes alter what reaches regulatory_provisions: the Marrickville section-heading fix changes every clause ref that council produces, and the legislation monitor now WRITES last_checked on a path that previously wrote nothing. Critical rather than Standard because a wrong ref is a citation a planner cannot resolve, and because the schema change is live in production ahead of the merge.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-69; python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-70
falsifiable_check.fails_when: DQ-69 returns more than 1. It counts active SEPPs/LEPs not checked within 14 days and was 26 of 26 before this branch (max(last_checked) = 2026-06-08, 67 days). It is 1 after, and that 1 is wingecarribee_lep_2010, which carries no pco_instrument_id and is deliberately NOT stamped. Only the monitor actually running moves this number; no code edit can. DQ-70 is the new outcome gate and is expected to stay RED at 595 - it is opened by this branch, not closed by it.

pre_impl.existing_data: instrument_registry: 26 active instruments, 25 with pco_instrument_id, 1 without. dcp_chapter_registry: 564 active, 206 hash-matched, 10 drifted, 348 with no recorded extraction hash; 655 rows total, 35 columns before migration 066 and 37 after. dcp_review_queue: 19,649 rows ever, 19,199 with fidelity_status, 12 with fidelity_source_quote.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The branch name says 'schedule'. It was never a scheduling problem. The monitor crashed at import on every cycle because #504 added refresh_runbook and never added the COPY, proven by running it on the live machine. Fly billing had also lapsed - a second, independent cause. A third followed: even once running, it recorded nothing.
pre_impl.prior_art: Extended the EXISTING image-completeness test rather than adding one; its from-scripts.X regex could not see the Fly image's flat COPY layout, which is why this shipped. Extended the EXISTING legislation-monitor and smart-monitor test modules for the same reason. No alert-state table existed anywhere (grepped scripts/, services/, migrations/, DB_SCHEMA.md), so migration 066 adds two columns to the registry row that already holds this chapter's operational state rather than opening a parallel table.

functions.name: check_instrument
functions.input: an instrument PCO did not list as amended, on the PCO path
functions.output: records last_checked when the instrument carries a pco_instrument_id (PCO's export lists every amended instrument, so absence is an affirmative confirmation); records NOTHING when it does not, because silence about an uncovered instrument means nothing
functions.if_none: the previous early return wrote nothing at all, so a run reporting 'Checked: 26' left last_checked frozen and no currency claim could be dated

functions.name: split_page_at_headings
functions.input: one page of text and the council's section regex
functions.output: [text before the first heading, then one block per heading]; returns [text] unchanged for 0- and 1-heading pages so non-split pages are bit-identical to before
functions.if_none: one heading per page survived, so a page holding 2.11.3/2.11.4/2.11.4.1 yielded only 2.11.3 and the other clauses collided onto it

functions.name: stuck_review_line
functions.input: a chapter flagged 53 days ago whose queue rows were rebuilt last night
functions.output: 'flagged 53d ago' - aged from the chapter flag, never from dcp_review_queue.created_at
functions.if_none: the alert printed 'stuck >48h' and 'oldest 1d' in the same message, because the nightly re-extract deletes and re-inserts the rows it was ageing

functions.name: unalerted_suspects
functions.input: suspect chapters plus the keys already alerted
functions.output: only those whose (content_hash, reason) is new or changed
functions.if_none: the same two chapters alerted byte-identically for 13 consecutive days and the channel stopped being read

functions.name: fetch_ocr_page_texts
functions.input: an OCR endpoint that stops responding
functions.output: gives up after OCR_READ_TIMEOUT (120s) instead of 1800s
functions.if_none: a scalar requests timeout is the gap BETWEEN BYTES, not a total deadline; a live socket was measured open 2472s against timeout=1800

values.read_at: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-69 against production, before and after, 2026-08-14
values.if_missing: without it, 'the monitor is fixed' rests on the code compiling rather than on the monitor having run

values.value: Marrickville gate: section coverage 632/730 = 86.6%, 0 of 83 chapters collapsed, 0 TIMEOUT, 0 ERROR, 0 unmeasured

queries.query: UPDATE instrument_registry SET last_checked = %s, check_failures = 0 WHERE instrument_key = %s
queries.scoped_by: instrument_key, single row, only when source='pco' AND the instrument carries a pco_instrument_id
queries.risk_if_unscoped: stamping an instrument PCO does not cover would fabricate a confirmation - we would record having checked something we cannot see

queries.query: UPDATE dcp_chapter_registry SET last_suspect_alert_key = %s, last_suspect_alert_at = NOW() WHERE council = %s AND chapter_key = %s
queries.scoped_by: (council, chapter_key), written only AFTER a successful Telegram send
queries.risk_if_unscoped: recording before the send would swallow a failed push - the condition would be marked as reported and never alert again

break_it.scenario: PCO reports no changes, which is the normal case, and the monitor is dead.
break_it.what_happens: Before: identical to a healthy run - silence. After: DQ-69 rises above 1 within 14 days.
break_it.how: last_checked is now written on the no-change path, so absence of movement is evidence of absence of running

break_it.scenario: A chapter's PDF is unchanged but its failure mode gets worse.
break_it.what_happens: Hash-only alert keying would silence it.
break_it.how: the key is (content_hash, reason); mutation-verified - hash-only keying fails test_a_changed_FAILURE_MODE_re_alerts_on_the_same_pdf

break_it.scenario: Two chapters share a content_hash and a reason, and only one has been alerted about.
break_it.what_happens: A global key lookup silences the second, which nobody has been told about.
break_it.how: lookup is per (council, chapter_key). ⚠ The FIRST version of this test used two chapters with different keys and could NOT distinguish the two behaviours - it passed against the global mutation. The discriminating case was added and is recorded here rather than quietly swapped in

break_it.scenario: The OCR endpoint dribbles bytes forever instead of stopping.
break_it.what_happens: The nightly extraction hangs indefinitely at 0% CPU, looking exactly like work in progress.
break_it.how: NOT FIXED and deliberately not asserted. Three in-thread mechanisms were built and measured and all three failed: a clock between 64KB chunks never runs; iter_content(None) reads to EOF; a Timer closing resp.raw does not unblock a recv on Windows. Bounding this needs an external subprocess cap - tracked as P6.0. A test for a behaviour the code cannot have would be a test that lies

mutation_analysis: Every behavioural change was mutation-verified in both directions and two mutations exposed weak tests, which is recorded rather than hidden. legislation_monitor: forcing the confirmed flag True fails the uncovered-instrument and other-sources tests (fabricated confirmation); forcing it False fails the covered-instrument test (the original bug). watchdog: ageing from a queue-derived 0 fails two tests, including one asserting a genuinely 2-day-old stall still reads as 2 days, so the fix cannot be 'print a big number'. alert dedup: hash-only keying goes red; the per-chapter-vs-global mutation initially PASSED and the test was strengthened until it failed. Marrickville: relaxing the <2 split guard, running each block to end-of-page, and emptying MULTI_HEADING_COUNCILS each go red. OCR: restoring the scalar timeout makes the silent-server test wait 120s against a 2s read timeout. ⚠ Two of the OCR tests originally passed against conftest_mocks' suite-wide `requests` stub - a MagicMock that answers instantly - so they exercised nothing; they now restore the genuine module and the trap is documented in the helper. The existing test_ocr_fallback fakes had the same defect after the streaming change and were repaired until swapping a 503 to a 200 turns test_non_200_returns_none red.
residual_risk: DQ-70 is opened RED at 595 and not closed here: those served provisions came from a PDF version we no longer hold, and only re-extracting the 10 drifted chapters clears it. 348 further chapters never recorded an extraction hash, so for those the question cannot be asked at all - a larger gap needing its own row. Source-quote verification has run on 12 of 19,649 queue rows (0.06%) because dcp_fidelity_gate is gated on AI_EXTRACTION, which also swaps the whole deterministic extractor for an LLM path - decoupling those is unstarted. The Marrickville coverage figure compares against the previous pipeline's output, not the source PDFs, so 86.6% means 'recovers the old corpus' and that corpus carries known errors; 98 section numbers were not recovered and are logged, not chased, per the stop line. The OCR dribble case is unbounded. r2_monitor.py, intelligence_brief.py and generate_conveyancing_report.py carry the same scalar-timeout assumption and are untouched. The deploy directory still holds hand-synced byte-copies of legislation_monitor.py and pco_client.py with no drift check.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Migration 066 is additive, nullable, IF NOT EXISTS, and was already applied to production and verified (35 -> 37 columns, exactly the two intended). No backfill by design.
post_merge.secrets: None added to the repo. TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID were reset on the Fly machine from the working Railway values because the Fly copy was returning HTTP 404; the values were piped between services and never printed.
post_merge.other_repo: No, but the Fly app plotdetect-legislation-monitor was redeployed from this branch's Dockerfile ahead of the merge, and the monitor was run manually to confirm: Checked 26, Changed 0, DB errors 0, telegram sent OK (200).
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes. Re-run DQ-69 a week after merge - it must still be 1. If it climbs to 26 the Fly loop has stopped again and the import fix was not the whole story.
